name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
summary: A Democrat who answered the Great Depression with the New Deal: banking and securities regulation, work relief, Social Security, labor-rights and wage-and-hours laws, public power through the TVA, and higher taxes on large incomes, always defending private enterprise and constitutional democracy. He moved the United States from neutrality toward aid to the Allies, led it in World War II, ordered the removal of Japanese Americans from the West Coast, and made a postwar United Nations a central goal.

notes: Answers rest on his own speeches and messages (1932-1945) and on the record of laws and orders he signed. Where views changed, the later position is used: his 1932 pledge to balance the budget gave way to deficit-financed relief; peacetime neutrality gave way to aid to the Allies and a call for a world organization. His 1937 letter held that collective bargaining cannot be transplanted into the public service and that strikes of federal employees are intolerable; his support for unions applies to private-sector workers. One answer is inferred (marked 'Inferred:') and is low confidence. No position was recorded for many cultural, religious and gender statements; none were guessed. Later pass 2026-11-13 (rules 7): sources tagged by kind (executive orders, acts and the court bill are actions); the four answers that rested only on Wikipedia pages now cite primary texts: tax-inheritance (1935 tax message, +2 high), freedom-to-discriminate (Executive Order 8802), unlimited-reelection and term-limits (the 1940 acceptance of a third nomination); answers that cited both actions and words were cut to the actions, with history. New answers from the Miller Center chats: money-backed-by-precious-metals, pay-off-national-debt, decent-living-guarantee and job-guarantee (second Bill of Rights, 1944), wealth concentration. Ships of the Seven Seas (Gutenberg 72859), whose 1924 introduction Roosevelt wrote, is cited for nation-first.
